title: Exclusive Time of Functions
summary: Given a list of logs where each log entry specifies a function ID, whether the function started or ended, and the timestamp, calculate the total exclusive execution time for each function ID.
statement: Given a list of logs where each log entry specifies a function ID, whether the function started or ended, and the timestamp, calculate the total exclusive execution time for each function ID. The logs are formatted as "{function_id}:{"start" | "end"}:{timestamp}". The exclusive time for a function is the sum of all the time units it executed, including any recursive calls. The result should be an array where the value at the i^th index corresponds to the exclusive execution time of the function with ID i.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100; logs form one valid single-threaded call stack.
An end timestamp is inclusive, and function IDs range from 0 through n-1.
hints: Only the function on top of the call stack executes.
Charge elapsed time at every event, accounting for inclusive end events.
Pause the old top on start; finish and pop on end; move previous to end+1.
The previous timestamp marks the first uncharged unit, so every unit is assigned exactly once.
editorial: The previous timestamp marks the first uncharged unit, so every unit is assigned exactly once.

tests.explanation: Function 0 runs for units 0-1 and 6; function 1 runs for units 2-5.
Recursive calls share the same function ID, whose exclusive units total seven.
